{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABa2dPVQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhEcQEM", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 107, "title": "Implement i486 4 KiB paging, page faults, and TLB coherency for PC-9821Ap protected-mode DOS guests", "body": "## Problem

A user booting a privately held PC-98 HDD image named `aliceY3.hdi` with **PC-9821Ap DOS** / **IDE · HDI boot** reports the next emulator stop:

```text
unsupported paging transition
```

Earlier compatibility milestones completed `MOV r32, CRn` ([#97](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/issues/97)), `MOV CRn, r32` ([#99](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/issues/99)), paging-disabled protected mode `PE=1 PG=0` ([#101](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/issues/101)), STR/LTR/TSS initialization ([#103](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/issues/103)), and CLTS / CR0.TS/#NM ([#105](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/issues/105)). The latest original Rust core **explicitly rejects CR0.PG=1** in [`Cpu::extended`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/cpu.rs) to avoid falsely claiming page translation. [The protected-mode roadmap](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/protected-mode.md) also identifies paging, CR2 and TLB as a missing independent memory-management subsystem.

The user has confirmed the **`unsupported paging transition`** message on their local HDD. This is meaningful evidence that execution reached the paging boundary, **not evidence that subsequent instructions, a DOS extender, FPU, Windows or the complete game will run**. The original disk, guest CPU trace, image checksum and legal status have not been independently inspected by the implementing agent.

## Expected outcome

Implement a **cohesive, original-Rust i386/i486-style 32-bit two-level 4 KiB paging subsystem** for the existing PC-9821Ap protected-mode CPU. A valid transition from `CR0.PE=1, PG=0` to **`PE=1, PG=1`** must enable real linear-to-physical translations through CR3, guest page directories and guest page tables. Every relevant CPU physical-memory access class must use the appropriate translation, page protection, accessed/dirty accounting, restartable **#PF** delivery, and TLB invalidation. Support transition back to non-paging mode.

**Do not fake paging** by accepting PG while continuing identity-addressing; do not assume every guest uses identity-mapped linear addresses. Keep Windows and speculative OS/DPMI/task-switch features out of scope. Preserve CPU, PC-98 device, DOS and browser regressions. The exact private HDD is *optional validation only* and never a mandatory fixture.

### Implementation architecture and scope

1. **CR0/CR3 transitions and policy.** Permit valid `PE=1, PG=1` transitions via `MOV CR0,r32` with i486 reserved/fixed-bit and PG-requires-PE checks; `MOV r32,CR0` / `SMSW` readback must reflect the actual state. Preserve CR0.TS, ET, EM, MP, CD/NW/NE and existing protected segment caches. `MOV CR3,r32` selects an actual page-directory physical base; validate defined/reserved bits according to an independently selected 486 contract. Disabling PG must restore the prior unpaged linear->physical mapping without corrupting caches or guest-visible state. Keep VM/V30 and Ap real-mode behavior unchanged.
2. **Translation and physical bus integration.** Implement two-level 32-bit paging: CR3 page-directory base, PDE/PTE lookup, 4 KiB frames, present and 486-valid access/reserved bits, 32-bit linear address assembly, page offset, and page crossing. Translate **instruction fetch, data reads/writes, stack operations, descriptor/table fetches and updates, protected IDT/GDT/LDT/TSS references, interrupt/fault frames, read-modify-write and DMA-vs-CPU memory semantics** in the correct places. Page-table walks use **physical** addresses via the existing bus, never recursively translated addresses. DMA/device-originated access must retain its hardware physical-address semantics unless independent hardware specifications say otherwise. Preserve the existing PC-98 memory map, RAM, VRAM/device I/O behavior and A20 policy; do not substitute IBM AT assumptions or blindly mask/identity-map out-of-range addresses. Reads/writes crossing a page boundary must translate each affected linear page.
3. **Permissions and architectural metadata.** Model PDE/PTE Present, R/W and U/S permissions across both levels, guest CPL/supervisor accesses within the currently supported ring-0 execution and correct `CR0.WP` behavior for the selected i486 model; enforce protection even when the virtual address is valid but the mapping/permissions are not. Update architectural Accessed/Dirty bits at the proper points and with the correct exceptions/restart state; do not overwrite unrecognized reserved flags. Handle instruction fetch and stack/descriptor accesses, data width and operand-address overrides. Full CPL3 task/privilege switching remains a **separate feature**; nevertheless build access-checking helpers usable by eventual nonzero-CPL support, with unit fixtures for access levels.
4. **Faults, CR2 and restart.** Deliver page faults through the **existing protected-mode IDT** as interrupt vector 14 with correct pushed error code (`P`, `W/R`, `U/S`, and selected 486-era supported fields; do not invent modern NX/instruction-fetch bits). CR2 must receive the correct faulting **linear** address and `MOV r32,CR2` must read it back. Guest handlers must be able to correct a nonpresent mapping or permissions and IRET/IRETD to **retry the original faulting instruction** without skipping/duplicating writes, consuming a wrong instruction pointer, or corrupting the frame. Include page faults during page walks, instruction fetch, descriptor access, stack frame creation and fault delivery, plus a bounded, accurate nested-fault/double/triple-fault diagnostic. Prevent partial mutation of CPU, RAM and memory-mapped device latches for a rejected operation to the extent required by correct 486 ordering.
5. **TLB and invalidation.** Implement coherent semantics for CR3 reload, toggling CR0.PG and `INVLPG` (`0F 01 /7`) including privilege and operand validation; use an original TLB or a documented uncached equivalent if it **preserves architectural observable stale-mapping/invalidation behavior**. Distinguish guest changes to page tables from explicit invalidation; don't make accidental host caching deterministically wrong. Include A/D bookkeeping across hit/miss, write-protect and fault-retry scenarios. Treat INVD/WBINVD and unsupported cache controls honestly; do not falsely report unrelated cache fidelity.
6. **Architecture and safety.** Use independent Intel 80386/486 manuals and existing original Rust CPU/bus contracts. No copied/translated/forked emulator or CPU core and no emulation/chip dependency. Do **not** silently enable 4 MiB PSE pages, PAE, virtual-8086, complete TSS task switching, ring-3 OS operation, DOS extenders or Windows support without separate justified tasks. At all unsupported boundaries produce meaningful, bounded CPU diagnostics rather than guest-visible fabricated success or an indefinite hang.

### Repro context and legal boundaries

User-observed sequence:
- `aliceY3.hdi` was initially accidentally mounted as floppy, then as IDE HDI in the Ap profile.
- Real-mode `0F 20` and `0F 22` blocked, both implemented in prior tasks.
- Valid `CR0.PE=1, PG=0` protected execution was needed and implemented.
- STR/LTR, then CLTS, were needed and implemented.
- **Current message:** `unsupported paging transition` after those milestones.

The error string alone does not supply the exact CR0 value or following guest operation, so do not extrapolate the next blocker. If a lawful private local copy of `aliceY3.hdi` is available to the implementer, a bounded diagnostic can check its actual CR0 transition and the next observed behavior. **Do not fetch, require, attach, upload, commit, include in CI/Pages/artifacts, or redistribute that private HDD or its contents**, full memory dumps, copyrighted code disassembly, BIOS/ROM/font data or game assets. The user will continue testing with their own copy locally.

Source and process:
- [CPU and control-register state](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/cpu.rs)
- [Protected-mode implementation](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/cpu/protected.rs)
- [Protected-mode limits and milestone roadmap](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/protected-mode.md)
- [DOS compatibility and private HDD diagnostic procedure](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/dos-compatibility.md)
- [Development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) / [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md).

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Reproduce the baseline** `unsupported paging transition` with an independently authored, MIT-licensed original CPU boot guest, **not `aliceY3.hdi`**, then demonstrate that real `PE=1, PG=1` execution passes on the new interpreter. The guest must use a **non-identity mapping** so falsely accepting PG cannot pass.
- [ ] Demonstrate a realistic complete **paging enable -> paged protected-code execution -> paging disable** cycle with correct CR0/CR3/CR2 readbacks, instruction fetch, code/data and stack addresses, and 16-/32-bit protected segment offsets. Use the existing PC-98 bus and guest instructions, not host-side CPU result synthesis.
- [ ] Native tests independently verify PDE/PTE lookup and 4 KiB boundary crossing, present/protection/reserved-bit policy, R/W + U/S permission combination, `CR0.WP`, Accessed/Dirty timing, page walks from physical RAM, A20 and PC-98 RAM/MMIO/ROM mapping, read/write/execute/cross-page spans, descriptor and exception-stack accesses. Explicitly verify DMA remains appropriately physical and does not inherit CPU virtual translations.
- [ ] `#PF` tests verify precise CR2 faulting linear addresses, architectural error code bits, restartable CS:EIP/EFLAGS/stack frames, IRET retry after guest handler changes PDE/PTE, nested page-fault handling and bounded double/triple fault outcomes, including cases where faults occur while translating instruction bytes, stack, GDT/IDT/TSS, or accessing page-table memory. Check CPU/RAM/EGC and other device latch state to avoid invalid partial side effects.
- [ ] Verify TLB/invalidation semantics across CR3 writes and reloads, PG enable/disable and `INVLPG` for present/nonpresent or modified mappings, including invalid encodings and privilege faults. No ungrounded claim of real i486 cache cycle accuracy.
- [ ] Add an original, explicitly redistributable, checksum-pinned, reproducible MIT guest fixture exercising nonidentity translation and page-fault recovery with a **guest-generated PASS marker and deterministic register/memory guards**. Execute it with actual Rust code in native/headless tests **and production Wasm in Chromium** for both `/` and `/pc98-rust/`, cold boot and reset. Browser must not substitute CPU execution with JavaScript assertions.
- [ ] Preserve all existing VM/V30, Ap real-mode and protected/TSS/CLTS, BIOS, PIC/PIT/FDC/IDE, PC-98 graphics/sound, FreeDOS/ADV98/98VIDEOP, Star Trail/HelloWorld and asset regressions. Run and record fixture preparation, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, production Rust/Wasm build/publication audit and complete real-Wasm Chromium suite **before merge**. No private software, proprietary ROM/font, external emulator core or suspicious dependency enters the repository.
- [ ] Update `docs/protected-mode.md`, `docs/hardware.md` and DOS compatibility docs with a transparent table of **implemented versus unsupported** i486 paging features, limitations (only 4 KiB two-level 32-bit paging, bounded CPL0, no PAE/PSE unless explicitly justified), exact test commands and validation evidence, and a concise grouped follow-up plan for any *actually demonstrated* remaining incompatibilities. If partial implementation cannot satisfy the acceptance contract, **keep this Issue open** or create a correctly scoped follow-up rather than closing it as full paging completion.
- [ ] Optional private `aliceY3.hdi` local retest, when lawfully accessible, checks progression beyond the actual PG transition and only records short CPU-level diagnostic metadata/next blocker. If inaccessible, state clearly **not retested**; do not claim that the commercial game boots or is playable.

**Every mandatory pre-merge criterion must be executable automatically with redistributable media and the original Rust/Wasm implementation.** No human game playthrough, private HDD image, physical PC-98 machine, remote published-site validation or post-merge check may become a pre-merge blocker. Follow the repository's English Issue/PR/review process and AI review expectations.

## Optional validation

Locally retest a lawfully held `aliceY3.hdi` without sharing it; compare additional 486 edge behavior to primary Intel documentation and file **separate `task` Issues** only for independently reproduced, cohesive follow-up subsystems. No Windows compatibility requested.

## Required post-merge verification

None. A later GitHub Pages/deployment or manual-game discrepancy belongs in a separate operational/compatibility `task` Issue and does not block this PR.
